column1: What is the fundamental problem every firearm operating system must solve?
column2: Safely harness and redirect the violent energy of cartridge ignition to cycle the action (extract, cock, chamber) while maintaining structural integrity and operator safety, given chamber pressures of 50,000–65,000 psi.

column1: Why is simple blowback limited to cartridges under ~35,000 psi?
column2: The breech is unlocked throughout firing and held closed only by bolt mass and spring resistance; higher pressures would require prohibitively heavy bolts (e.g., 20+ lbs for 7.62x51mm) to delay opening safely.

column1: What mechanical principle does delayed blowback use to permit higher-pressure cartridges without excessive bolt mass?
column2: Kinematic mechanical disadvantage (rollers, levers, radial cams, or gas hesitation rings) that multiplies effective bolt inertia by a factor K = 3–6.

column1: What is the momentum equilibrium invariant across the breech interface in firearm design?
column2: ∫₀^t_bore P(t)·A_bore dt = m_bullet·v_bullet + m_gas·v_gas = m_breech·v_breech — the pressure-time impulse on the bore must equal the momentum imparted to the breech.

column1: What happens if breech unsealing occurs while chamber pressure P(t) > 5 MPa?
column2: The cartridge case wall loses radial support from the steel chamber wall, causing violent hoop stress rupture and hot gas escape into the receiver.

column1: How do locked-breech recoil systems differ from simple blowback in their unlocking timing?
column2: Barrel and bolt remain rigidly mechanically interlocked for the initial 2–5 mm of rearward travel until a cam or link tilts or rotates the barrel, releasing the bolt only after bullet exit.

column1: Why are propellants classified as deflagrating rather than detonating materials?
column2: They burn subsonic to the flame front, producing a controlled, progressive pressure rise rather than a supersonic shock wave (detonation).

column1: How does grain geometry affect propellant burn rate progression (spherical vs. perforated cylindrical grains)?
column2: Spherical grains burn progressively slower as surface area decreases with the cube of radius; perforated cylindrical grains burn progressively faster because the expanding inner perforation increases total surface area as the outer diameter shrinks.

column1: What is the 'positive interlock principle' in firearm safety design?
column2: The firing pin/striker must be physically blocked from contacting the primer by a solid mechanical barrier at all times, except when the trigger is deliberately pulled through its full stroke.

column1: What is the function of a transfer bar / hammer block safety?
column2: A movable steel bar must be held in position between hammer and firing pin by active trigger pull; at rest, the hammer strikes an immovable frame stop instead of the firing pin, preventing discharge from impact.

column1: What does the trigger bar disconnector prevent, and how?
column2: It prevents automatic doubling or out-of-battery ignition by using a cammed lever that mechanically decouples the trigger bar from the sear whenever the slide or bolt carrier moves rearward out of full battery.

column1: In chamber headspace verification, why must the extractor and ejector be stripped before gauging?
column2: An installed spring-loaded ejector exerts forward pressure against the headspace gauge, masking the true headspace reading and producing an inaccurate measurement.
